For a 50-person Indian company, I’d take these three into the final RFQ. There isn’t enough public pricing to make a defensible “best-value” winner; the key is the all-in fee structure.

Provider	Purchase case	Trade-offs / terms to verify
Thomas Cook India Business Travel	Strong SME fit; handles air, hotels, rail, cars, visas, forex and insurance. Its corporate operation explicitly serves SMEs and offers booking, expense and GST tools. 
Thomas Cook
+1
	Quote required. Get per-ticket/service fees, hotel markup, reissue/cancellation charges, SLA and implementation cost in writing. 24/7 emergency support is offered. 
Thomas Cook

FCM Travel / Corporate Traveller	Strong managed-service option with 24/7 support, policy controls, analytics and traveller-risk tools; Corporate Traveller is FCM’s SME-focused Indian brand. 
FCM Travel
+1
	FCM says its core focus is larger programmes; confirm Corporate Traveller eligibility, minimum annual spend and dedicated-account coverage. 
FCM Travel

American Express GBT + Business Travel Account	Useful where centralized air-spend control matters: one bill, reconciliation and up to 51 days payment period. 
American Express
	BTA works through your TMC, so compare the TMC + Amex costs together; fees are quote-based. 
American Express

Before paying: require a 12-month total-cost quote, including GST, transaction fees, markups, after-hours fees, cancellation/reissue rules, credit terms, SLA/service credits, implementation, and exit/data-export terms.
